claim: The proximal and distal femur epiphyses of mice are both weight-bearing structures derived from chondrocytes but differ in development.
source: The proximal and distal femur epiphyses of mice are both weight-bearing structures derived from chondrocytes but differ in development.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing anatomical and developmental characteristics of femur epiphyses.

claim: Mineralization at the distal epiphysis occurs in an osteoblast-rich secondary ossification center (SOC).
source: Mineralization at the distal epiphysis occurs in an osteoblast-rich secondary ossification center (SOC), while the chondrocytes of the proximal femur head (FH), in particular, are directly mineralized.
evidence: This statement is supported by the manuscript's histological and imaging data showing SOC formation at the distal femur.

claim: Chondrocytes of the proximal femur head are directly mineralized.
source: Mineralization at the distal epiphysis occurs in an osteoblast-rich secondary ossification center (SOC), while the chondrocytes of the proximal femur head (FH), in particular, are directly mineralized.
evidence: This is supported by histological data and imaging showing direct mineralization without SOC formation at the FH.

claim: Thyroid hormone (TH) plays important roles in distal knee SOC formation.
source: Thyroid hormone (TH) plays important roles in distal knee SOC formation, but whether TH also affects proximal FH development remains unexplored.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and data in the manuscript.

claim: TH controls chondrocyte maturation and mineralization at the FH in vivo.
source: Here, we found that TH controls chondrocyte maturation and mineralization at the FH in vivo through studies in thyroid stimulating hormone receptor (Tshr-/-) hypothyroid mice by X-ray, histology, transcriptional profiling, and immunofluorescence staining.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental approaches described in the manuscript including X-ray, histology, transcriptional profiling, and immunofluorescence.

claim: TH regulates expression of genes that modulate mineralization (Ibsp, Bglap2, Dmp1, Spp1, and Alpl) both in vivo and in vitro.
source: Both in vivo and in vitro studies conducted in ATDC5 chondrocyte progenitors concur that TH regulates expression of genes that modulate mineralization (Ibsp, Bglap2, Dmp1, Spp1, and Alpl).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data from both in vivo mouse studies and in vitro ATDC5 cell culture experiments.

claim: There are differences in prominent transcription factor regulation of genes involved in proximal FH cartilage calcification versus endochondral ossification at the distal femur.
source: Our work also delineates differences in prominent transcription factor regulation of genes involved in the different mechanisms leading to proximal FH cartilage calcification and endochondral ossification at the distal femur.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing differential expression of transcription factors and knockdown experiments in ATDC5 cells.

claim: Most bones are formed by endochondral ossification where condensed mesenchymal stem cells proliferate and differentiate into chondrocytes.
source: Most bones are formed by endochondral ossification where condensed mesenchymal stem cells proliferate and differentiate into chondrocytes.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about bone development.

claim: In mice, the POC has been established to occur during embryonic development day (E) E14.5–15.5.
source: In mice, the POC has been established to occur during embryonic development day (E) E14.5–15.5 while the secondary ossification center (SOC) forms at approximately postnatal day (P) P5–7 at the epiphyseal ends (Mackie et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mackie et al., 2011.

claim: The secondary ossification center (SOC) forms at approximately postnatal day (P) P5–7 at the epiphyseal ends in mice.
source: In mice, the POC has been established to occur during embryonic development day (E) E14.5–15.5 while the secondary ossification center (SOC) forms at approximately postnatal day (P) P5–7 at the epiphyseal ends (Mackie et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mackie et al., 2011.

claim: Early chondrocytes are characterized by expression of collagen, type 2, alpha 1 (COL2A1), and aggrecan (ACAN).
source: Early chondrocytes which are characterized by expression of collagen, type 2, alpha 1 (COL2A1), and aggrecan (ACAN) undergo proliferation, withdraw from the cell cycle, and differentiate into pre-hypertrophic chondrocytes expressing Indian hedgehog (IHH) and Sp7 transcription factor (SP7).
evidence: This is established knowledge about chondrocyte markers.

claim: Pre-hypertrophic chondrocytes express Indian hedgehog (IHH) and Sp7 transcription factor (SP7).
source: Early chondrocytes which are characterized by expression of collagen, type 2, alpha 1 (COL2A1), and aggrecan (ACAN) undergo proliferation, withdraw from the cell cycle, and differentiate into pre-hypertrophic chondrocytes expressing Indian hedgehog (IHH) and Sp7 transcription factor (SP7).
evidence: This is established knowledge about chondrocyte differentiation markers.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes express high levels of a cartilage matrix consisting of matrix metalloproteinase 13 (MMP13) and collagen, type 10, alpha 1 (COL10A1).
source: Hypertrophic chondrocytes express high levels of a cartilage matrix consisting of matrix metalloproteinase 13 (MMP13) and collagen, type 10, alpha 1 (COL10A1), creating a template for bone formation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about hypertrophic chondrocyte markers.

claim: Expression of vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) leads to invasion by capillaries, which allows the influx of osteoblasts, osteoclasts, and bone marrow cells to replace the cartilage matrix with mineralized bone.
source: Expression of vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) subsequently leads to invasion by capillaries, which allows the influx of osteoblasts, osteoclasts, and bone marrow cells to replace the cartilage matrix with mineralized bone (Li and Dong, 2016; Mackie et al., 2011; Takarada et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li and Dong, 2016; Mackie et al., 2011; Takarada et al., 2016.

claim: The growth plate is responsible for longitudinal skeletal growth.
source: The growth plate is responsible for longitudinal skeletal growth and skeletal maturity is reached when the POC and SOC meet (Mackie et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Mackie et al., 2011.

claim: Skeletal maturity is reached when the POC and SOC meet.
source: The growth plate is responsible for longitudinal skeletal growth and skeletal maturity is reached when the POC and SOC meet (Mackie et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mackie et al., 2011.

claim: Optimal levels of TH peak simultaneously with the initiation of SOC formation.
source: Optimal levels of TH peak simultaneously with the initiation of SOC formation and are essential for its development (Aghajanian et al., 2017; Kim and Mohan, 2013; Xing et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aghajanian et al., 2017; Kim and Mohan, 2013; Xing et al., 2014.

claim: TH is essential for SOC development.
source: Optimal levels of TH peak simultaneously with the initiation of SOC formation and are essential for its development (Aghajanian et al., 2017; Kim and Mohan, 2013; Xing et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aghajanian et al., 2017; Kim and Mohan, 2013; Xing et al., 2014.

claim: Dysregulation in the amount of TH during skeletal development can lead to growth arrest and delayed bone formation in both humans and mice.
source: Dysregulation in the amount of TH during skeletal development can lead to growth arrest, and delayed bone formation in both humans and mice (Bassett et al., 2008; Gogakos et al., 2010; Kim and Mohan, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bassett et al., 2008; Gogakos et al., 2010; Kim and Mohan, 2013.

claim: TH regulates the development of the SOC through IHH signaling and SP7 activity.
source: We found that TH regulates the development of the SOC through IHH signaling and SP7 activity, and that TH is a major regulator of a number of key bone growth factors, including insulin-like growth factor-I (Mohan et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work by the authors' group.

claim: TH is a major regulator of a number of key bone growth factors, including insulin-like growth factor-I.
source: We found that TH regulates the development of the SOC through IHH signaling and SP7 activity, and that TH is a major regulator of a number of key bone growth factors, including insulin-like growth factor-I (Mohan et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mohan et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2006.

claim: TH-deficient Tshr-/- mice have severely compromised development of the epiphysis in both the femur and tibia at the knee joint.
source: We also established that TH-deficient Tshr-/- mice have severely compromised development of the epiphysis in both the femur and tibia at the knee joint, which is completely rescuable by TH treatment for 10 days when serum levels of TH rise in wild type mice (Xing et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xing et al., 2014.

claim: The epiphyseal defect in Tshr-/- mice is completely rescuable by TH treatment for 10 days when serum levels of TH rise in wild type mice.
source: We also established that TH-deficient Tshr-/- mice have severely compromised development of the epiphysis in both the femur and tibia at the knee joint, which is completely rescuable by TH treatment for 10 days when serum levels of TH rise in wild type mice (Xing et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xing et al., 2014.

claim: TH regulates SOC formation at the epiphysis of the distal femur and proximal tibia by a TH-induced chondrocyte-to-osteoblast transdifferentiation mechanism.
source: Additionally, we found that TH regulates SOC formation at the epiphysis of the distal femur and proximal tibia, by a TH-induced chondrocyte-to-osteoblast transdifferentiation mechanism (Aghajanian et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Aghajanian et al., 2017.

claim: Bone development culminates at a later timepoint in the proximal femur relative to the distal femur.
source: Previous studies have revealed that bone development culminates at a later timepoint in the proximal femur relative to the distal femur, suggesting a difference in developmental mechanisms (Patton and Kaufman, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Patton and Kaufman, 1995.

claim: The proximal and distal femur had different developmental patterns in terms of timing, vascular development, and ossification in mice.
source: A recent study in mice by Cole et al., 2013, found that the proximal and distal femur had different developmental patterns in terms of timing, vascular development, and ossification.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cole et al., 2013.

claim: At the distal epiphysis, the cartilage template was replaced by bone matrix via a chondrocyte-to-osteoblast transdifferentiation-mediated endochondral ossification process.
source: While the cartilage template at the distal epiphysis was replaced by bone matrix via a chondrocyte-to-osteoblast transdifferentiation-mediated endochondral ossification process, at the proximal femoral epiphysis cartilage was directly mineralized without the involvement of an SOC (Cole et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cole et al., 2013.

claim: At the proximal femoral epiphysis, cartilage was directly mineralized without the involvement of an SOC.
source: While the cartilage template at the distal epiphysis was replaced by bone matrix via a chondrocyte-to-osteoblast transdifferentiation-mediated endochondral ossification process, at the proximal femoral epiphysis cartilage was directly mineralized without the involvement of an SOC (Cole et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cole et al., 2013.

claim: A distinct gap was evident between the FH and acetabulum in Tshr-/- mice on day 21.
source: X-ray imaging of genotyped mice revealed that compared with the tight apposition of the FH with the acetabulum of the pelvic bone in Tshr+/-, a distinct gap was evident between the FH and acetabulum in Tshr-/- mice (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by X-ray imaging data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: All three of the proximal femur structures (greater trochanter, FH, and lesser trochanter) were underdeveloped in Tshr-/- injected with vehicle compared to Tshr+/- mice.
source: While all three of the proximal femur structures (greater trochanter, FH, and lesser trochanter) were underdeveloped in Tshr-/- injected with vehicle compared to Tshr+/- mice (Figure 1B), restoration of all three structures in Tshr-/- injected with T3/T4 indicates TH signaling also regulates development and mineralization of the proximal femur epiphysis (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by μCT imaging data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Restoration of all three proximal femur structures in Tshr-/- injected with T3/T4 indicates TH signaling regulates development and mineralization of the proximal femur epiphysis.
source: While all three of the proximal femur structures (greater trochanter, FH, and lesser trochanter) were underdeveloped in Tshr-/- injected with vehicle compared to Tshr+/- mice (Figure 1B), restoration of all three structures in Tshr-/- injected with T3/T4 indicates TH signaling also regulates development and mineralization of the proximal femur epiphysis (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by μCT imaging data shown in Figure 1C demonstrating rescue by TH treatment.

claim: There is a 10-day delay in the initiation of mineralization at the FH compared to the distal femoral epiphysis.
source: Our data revealed a 10-day delay in the initiation of mineralization at the FH compared to the distal femoral epiphysis (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by nano-CT imaging data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: The cartilage area was greater at the proximal FH in Tshr-/- mice relative to Tshr+/- controls.
source: Relative to Tshr+/- controls, the cartilage area was greater at the proximal FH in Tshr-/- mice (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by histology staining data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Alizarin red and Von Kossa mineral staining were only detected on day 21 of Tshr+/- controls in the proximal FH.
source: In the proximal FH, Alizarin red and Von Kossa mineral staining were only detected on day 21 of Tshr+/- controls (Figure 2C and D), which corroborates nano-CT results.
evidence: This is supported by histology staining data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Extensive mineral staining was seen at the distal femur SOC in euthyroid mice at both timepoints (P10 and P21).
source: Conversely, extensive mineral staining was seen at the distal femur SOC in euthyroid mice at both timepoints, but to a reduced extent in the distal femur SOC of Tshr-/- mice on day 21 (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is supported by histology staining data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Mineral staining was reduced in the distal femur SOC of Tshr-/- mice on day 21.
source: Conversely, extensive mineral staining was seen at the distal femur SOC in euthyroid mice at both timepoints, but to a reduced extent in the distal femur SOC of Tshr-/- mice on day 21 (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is supported by histology staining data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Positive staining for tartrate resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP, also known as ACP5) was found in the actively mineralizing region of distal femur SOC.
source: Interestingly, positive staining for tartrate resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP, also known as ACP5) was found in the actively mineralizing region of distal femur SOC (Figure 2E), which was also dependent on TH status.
evidence: This is supported by TRAP staining data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: TRAP staining in the distal femur SOC was dependent on TH status.
source: Interestingly, positive staining for tartrate resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP, also known as ACP5) was found in the actively mineralizing region of distal femur SOC (Figure 2E), which was also dependent on TH status.
evidence: This is supported by TRAP staining data shown in Figure 2E comparing different genotypes.

claim: TRAP staining was not detected in the FH of either genotype, even on day 21.
source: However, TRAP staining was not detected in the FH of either genotype, even on day 21.
evidence: This is supported by TRAP staining data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: A delay in maturation at both ends in day 10 hypothyroid femurs was evident by reduced mRNA levels of genes expressed in mature chondrocytes Ihh, Tnfsf11, Sp7, Col10a1, Alpl, and Mmp13.
source: A delay in maturation at both ends in day 10 hypothyroid femurs was evident by reduced mRNA levels of genes expressed in mature chondrocytes Ihh, Tnfsf11, Sp7, Col10a1, Alpl, and Mmp13 (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Markers of immature chondrocytes Shh and Sox9 were increased, but only significantly at the FH.
source: Moreover, markers of immature chondrocytes Shh and Sox9 were increased, but only significantly at the FH (Figure 3A and B), indicating a more substantial delay in maturation of FH chondrocytes on day 10.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: TH treatment increased Col10a1 expression in the distal femur but not proximal FH at day 10.
source: TH treatment increased Col10a1 expression in the distal femur but not proximal FH at day 10, further supporting a delay in chondrocyte maturation at the FH.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Expression levels of genes involved in mineralization, Ibsp, Spp1 and Acp5, were reduced at the distal femur of day 10 Tshr-/- mice.
source: Furthermore, while expression levels of genes involved in mineralization, Ibsp, Spp1 and Acp5, were reduced, Mgp expression was elevated at the distal femur of day 10 Tshr-/- mice, but none of these were affected in the FH (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Mgp expression was elevated at the distal femur of day 10 Tshr-/- mice.
source: Furthermore, while expression levels of genes involved in mineralization, Ibsp, Spp1 and Acp5, were reduced, Mgp expression was elevated at the distal femur of day 10 Tshr-/- mice, but none of these were affected in the FH (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Mineralization-related genes (Ibsp, Spp1, Acp5, Mgp) were not affected in the FH of day 10 Tshr-/- mice.
source: Furthermore, while expression levels of genes involved in mineralization, Ibsp, Spp1 and Acp5, were reduced, Mgp expression was elevated at the distal femur of day 10 Tshr-/- mice, but none of these were affected in the FH (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: In day 10 Tshr-/- femurs, the expression levels of Hif1a were unchanged at both the FH and distal femur.
source: Since others, and we, have shown a key role for hypoxia signaling in chondrocyte maturation (Cheng et al., 2016; Cheng et al., 2017; Schipani et al., 2001; Yellowley and Genetos, 2019), we measured expression of hypoxia signaling genes and found that in day 10 Tshr-/- femurs the expression levels of Hif1a were unchanged at both the FH and distal femur, while Epas1 and Vegfa were reduced at the FH and not restored by TH treatment (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Epas1 and Vegfa were reduced at the FH and not restored by TH treatment in day 10 Tshr-/- femurs.
source: Since others, and we, have shown a key role for hypoxia signaling in chondrocyte maturation (Cheng et al., 2016; Cheng et al., 2017; Schipani et al., 2001; Yellowley and Genetos, 2019), we measured expression of hypoxia signaling genes and found that in day 10 Tshr-/- femurs the expression levels of Hif1a were unchanged at both the FH and distal femur, while Epas1 and Vegfa were reduced at the FH and not restored by TH treatment (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Tgfa expression was negatively regulated by TH at the FH but not at the distal femur.
source: Tgfa expression was negatively regulated by TH at the FH but not at the distal femur (Figure 3A), thus suggesting region-specific effects of TH on the femur.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Expression levels of immature chondrocyte markers, Sox9 and Acan, were increased at both ends on day 21 in hypothyroid mice, yet reduced by TH treatment.
source: On day 21, femurs of hypothyroid mice continued to display profiles suggesting a delay in maturation. Expression levels of immature chondrocyte markers, Sox9 and Acan, were increased at both ends, yet reduced by TH treatment (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Col10a1 mRNA levels were reduced in the FH of Tshr-/- mice on day 21.
source: While Col2a1 mRNA levels were unchanged, Col10a1 mRNA levels were reduced in the FH of Tshr-/- mice (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Increased mRNA levels of Ihh in both proximal and distal femurs of Tshr-/- mice were restored to control levels by TH treatment.
source: Increased mRNA levels of Ihh in both proximal and distal femurs of Tshr-/- mice were also restored to control levels by TH treatment, thus suggesting a role for Ihh in chondrocyte maturation.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Alpl and Acp5 transcripts were reduced at the proximal FH but not distal femur of Tshr-/- mice at day 21 and rescued by TH.
source: Alpl and Acp5 transcripts were reduced at the proximal FH but not distal femur of Tshr-/- mice at day 21 and rescued by TH (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: TH treatment produced opposite effects on Ibsp expression at the two femoral sites in Tshr-/- mice on day 21.
source: TH treatment produced opposite effects on Ibsp expression at the two femoral sites in Tshr-/- mice on day 21.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The reduced Bglap2 mRNA levels at the proximal FH and distal femur of Tshr-/- mice at day 21 were rescued by TH treatment.
source: By contrast, the reduced Bglap2 mRNA levels at the proximal FH and distal femur of Tshr-/- mice at day 21 were rescued by TH treatment (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Expression levels of growth factors Bmp2 and Tnfrsf11b were elevated at both ends of the femur in Tshr-/- mice on day 21 and rescued by TH treatment.
source: Interestingly, expression levels of growth factors Bmp2 and Tnfrsf11b were elevated at both ends of the femur in Tshr-/- mice on day 21 and rescued by TH treatment (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Expression of Runx2 and Ctnnb1 was not affected at either FH or distal femur in Tshr-/- mice on day 21.
source: Although expression of Runx2 and Ctnnb1 was not affected at either FH or distal femur (Figure 3F), TH treatment increased their expression at the FH only.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: TH treatment increased Runx2 and Ctnnb1 expression at the FH only on day 21.
source: Although expression of Runx2 and Ctnnb1 was not affected at either FH or distal femur (Figure 3F), TH treatment increased their expression at the FH only.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The reduced expression of Ihh, Tnfsf11, Sp7, Mmp13, Ibsp, and Alpl at day 10 was consistent with the delayed maturation of chondrocytes at the proximal FH.
source: The reduced expression of Ihh, Tnfsf11, Sp7, Mmp13, Ibsp, and Alpl (Figure 3I) at day 10 was consistent with the delayed maturation of chondrocytes at the proximal FH.
evidence: This is an interpretation of RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: At day 21, many genes (Ihh, Tnfsf11, Sp7, Mmp13, Ibsp, Alpl) were expressed at higher levels in the FH compared to the distal femur.
source: However, at day 21, many of these genes were expressed at higher levels in the FH, a finding consistent with active mineralization occurring at this time.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: COL2A1 was present in chondrocytes of day 10 FH.
source: In the proximal FH, however, there was a delay in the expression of markers of chondrocyte differentiation as noted by the presence of COL2A1 in chondrocytes of day 10 FH, and subsequent replacement of COL2A1 with COL10A1 that persisted during active mineralization on day 17 (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4.

claim: COL2A1 was replaced with COL10A1 that persisted during active mineralization on day 17 in the FH.
source: In the proximal FH, however, there was a delay in the expression of markers of chondrocyte differentiation as noted by the presence of COL2A1 in chondrocytes of day 10 FH, and subsequent replacement of COL2A1 with COL10A1 that persisted during active mineralization on day 17 (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4.

claim: COL1A1 expression was not detected during active mineralization in the FH.
source: Remarkably, in contrast to the SOC, COL1A1 expression was not detected during active mineralization in the FH.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4.

claim: In Tshr-/- mice, the expression domain of COL2A1 was expanded at the FH.
source: In agreement with delayed chondrocyte maturation at the FH of Tshr-/- mice, the expression domain of COL2A1 was expanded, while COL10A1 was decreased compared with stage matched controls (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4.

claim: COL10A1 was decreased at the FH of Tshr-/- mice compared with stage matched controls.
source: In agreement with delayed chondrocyte maturation at the FH of Tshr-/- mice, the expression domain of COL2A1 was expanded, while COL10A1 was decreased compared with stage matched controls (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4.

claim: On day 10, MMP13 was largely expressed in a non-overlapping domain with COL2A1.
source: Immunostaining revealed that on day 10, MMP13 was largely expressed in a non-overlapping domain with COL2A1, while on days 17 and 21, MMP13 overlapped both COL2A1 and COL10A1 in chondrocytes, but minimally overlapped COL1A1 in bone, and remained expressed in FH of Tshr-/- mice (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5.

claim: On days 17 and 21, MMP13 overlapped both COL2A1 and COL10A1 in chondrocytes.
source: Immunostaining revealed that on day 10, MMP13 was largely expressed in a non-overlapping domain with COL2A1, while on days 17 and 21, MMP13 overlapped both COL2A1 and COL10A1 in chondrocytes, but minimally overlapped COL1A1 in bone, and remained expressed in FH of Tshr-/- mice (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5.

claim: MMP13 minimally overlapped COL1A1 in bone.
source: Immunostaining revealed that on day 10, MMP13 was largely expressed in a non-overlapping domain with COL2A1, while on days 17 and 21, MMP13 overlapped both COL2A1 and COL10A1 in chondrocytes, but minimally overlapped COL1A1 in bone, and remained expressed in FH of Tshr-/- mice (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5.

claim: MMP13 remained expressed in FH of Tshr-/- mice.
source: Immunostaining revealed that on day 10, MMP13 was largely expressed in a non-overlapping domain with COL2A1, while on days 17 and 21, MMP13 overlapped both COL2A1 and COL10A1 in chondrocytes, but minimally overlapped COL1A1 in bone, and remained expressed in FH of Tshr-/- mice (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5.

claim: MMP9 was detected in bone tissue of all samples including strong expression at the SOC.
source: MMP9 degrades collagens expressed by more mature chondrocytes (Stickens et al., 2004), and while it was detected in bone tissue of all samples including strong expression at the SOC, it was not expressed in FH chondrocytes (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5.

claim: MMP9 was not expressed in FH chondrocytes.
source: MMP9 degrades collagens expressed by more mature chondrocytes (Stickens et al., 2004), and while it was detected in bone tissue of all samples including strong expression at the SOC, it was not expressed in FH chondrocytes (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5.

claim: CAR2 was expressed in osteoblasts at the tibia SOC and in bone beneath the FH.
source: While we found expression of CAR2 in osteoblasts at the tibia SOC and in bone beneath the FH, we did not detect its expression in FH chondrocytes (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5.

claim: CAR2 was not detected in FH chondrocytes.
source: While we found expression of CAR2 in osteoblasts at the tibia SOC and in bone beneath the FH, we did not detect its expression in FH chondrocytes (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5.

claim: IBSP, BGLAP2, DMP1, and SPP1 were all expressed highly in the SOC and bone below the FH at all timepoints analyzed.
source: We also evaluated expression of non-collagenous extracellular matrix proteins involved in mineralization, IBSP, BGLAP2, DMP1, and SPP1. They were all expressed highly in the SOC and bone below the FH at all timepoints analyzed, and only BGLAP2 was found in day 10 FH.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Only BGLAP2 was found in day 10 FH among the non-collagenous extracellular matrix proteins (IBSP, BGLAP2, DMP1, SPP1).
source: We also evaluated expression of non-collagenous extracellular matrix proteins involved in mineralization, IBSP, BGLAP2, DMP1, and SPP1. They were all expressed highly in the SOC and bone below the FH at all timepoints analyzed, and only BGLAP2 was found in day 10 FH.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6.

claim: On days 17 and 21, BGLAP2 expression was lower in FH than in the bone matrix below the FH.
source: On days 17 and 21 BGLAP2 expression was lower in FH than in the bone matrix below the FH.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6.

claim: There was some positive signal for IBSP in the FH on days 17 and 21, but the signal intensity was much less than seen in the bone beneath the FH chondrocytes.
source: While there was some positive signal for IBSP in the FH on days 17 and 21, the signal intensity was much less than seen in the bone beneath the FH chondrocytes.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6.

claim: DMP1 was not detected in the FH at any of the days evaluated.
source: DMP1 was not detected in the FH at any of the days evaluated, and SPP1 was expressed at high level in mineralizing chondrocytes of Tshr+/- FH on day 17 (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6.

claim: SPP1 was expressed at high level in mineralizing chondrocytes of Tshr+/- FH on day 17.
source: DMP1 was not detected in the FH at any of the days evaluated, and SPP1 was expressed at high level in mineralizing chondrocytes of Tshr+/- FH on day 17 (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6.

claim: None of the mineralization factors (IBSP, BGLAP2, DMP1, SPP1) were expressed in Tshr-/- FH chondrocytes.
source: None of these mineralization factors were expressed in Tshr-/- FH chondrocytes.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6.

claim: ALPL activity was detected in bone and mineralizing regions of FH in Tshr+/- mice at days 17 and 21.
source: ALPL activity was detected in bone and mineralizing regions of FH in Tshr+/- mice at days 17 and 21 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by ALPL histochemistry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: SOX9 signal was limited to chondrocytes in all regions examined.
source: SOX9 signal was limited to chondrocytes in all regions examined.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Mature chondrocytes transdifferentiate into osteoblasts in the presence of an SP7 and DLX5 duo at the SOC of the distal femur.
source: Thus, we postulate that while mature chondrocytes transdifferentiate into osteoblasts in the presence of an SP7 and DLX5 duo, which produces bone matrix that promotes endochondral bone formation at the SOC of the distal femur, RUNX2 in the absence of SP7 may interact with DLX3 to promote terminal differentiation of mature chondrocytes and subsequent cartilage mineralization at the FH.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Chondrocyte-specific knockout of SP7 has been reported to result in expanded hypertrophic chondrocyte mineralization.
source: Chondrocyte-specific knockout of SP7 has been reported to result in expanded hypertrophic chondrocyte mineralization (Jing et al., 2014; Zhou et al., 2010), demonstrating that SP7 is not required for chondrocyte mineralization, and its timely absence may even affect the fate of RUNX2+ hypertrophic chondrocytes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jing et al., 2014; Zhou et al., 2010.
